spectrum, comorbidities and outcomes in patients with obesity"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;TUSHARA CH THESIS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003ETITLE\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECLINICAL SPECTRUM, COMORBIDITIES AND OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH OBESITY.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EINTRODUCTION:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EObesity is one of the most serious public health challenges of the 21st century. The problem is global and is steadily affecting many low and middle income countries, particularly in urban settings. The prevalence has increased at an alarming rate. Overweight and obese patients are more likely to develop diseases like diabetes and cardiovascular diseases at a younger age, the risks depend partly on the age of onset and on the duration of obesity. Obese patients suffer from both short-term and long-term health consequences.\u0026nbsp; \u003Cbr\u003EThe most significant health consequences of overweight and obesity are:\u003Cbr\u003Ecardiovascular diseases (mainly heart disease and stroke); \u003Cbr\u003EDiabetes; \u003Cbr\u003EMusculoskeletal disorders, especially osteoarthritis; and \u003Cbr\u003ECertain types of cancer (endometrial, breast and colon). \u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EThe fundamental cause of overweight and obesity is an energy imbalance between calories consumed and calories spent. \u003Cbr\u003EGlobal increases in overweight and obesity are attributable to a number of factors including: \u003Cbr\u003E• A global shift in the diet towards increased intake of energy-dense foods that are high in fat and sugars but low in vitamins, minerals and other healthy micronutrients; \u003Cbr\u003E• A trend towards decreased physical activity levels due to the increasing sedentary nature of many forms of recreation time, changing modes of transportation, and increasing urbanization.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E *Metabolic syndrome:*\u0026nbsp; \u003Cbr\u003EMetabolic syndrome is also known as metabolic syndrome X, syndrome X, insulin resistance syndrome, Reaven's syndrome is a combination of medical disorders that increase the risk of developing cardiovascular diseases and diabetes.\u0026nbsp; \u003Cbr\u003EAlthough the pathophysiology of this syndrome is incompletely understood, insulin resistance and abdominal obesity are central to many of the metabolic perturbations. Based on existing estimates the metabolic syndrome affects- nearly 1\/4th of the populations in developed countries. Prevalence of the metabolic syndrome is increasing in developing countries, including India.\u003Cbr\u003EInsulin resistance and resulting hyperinsulinemia have been implicated in the development of glucose intolerance (and progression to type 2 diabetes), hypertriglyceridemia, hypertension, polycystic ovary syndrome, hypercoagulability and vascular inflammation, as well as the eventual development of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease manifested as myocardial infarction, stroke and myriad end organ diseases. \u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EThere are other concerns as well that should be mentioned. Metabolic syndrome is associated with fat accumulation in the liver (fatty liver), resulting in inflammation and the potential for cirrhosis. The kidneys can also be affected, as there is an association with microalbuminuria the leaking of protein into the urine, a subtle but clear indication of kidney damage.\u0026nbsp; \u003Cbr\u003EOther problems associated with metabolic syndrome include obstructive sleep apnea, polycystic ovary syndrome, increased risk of dementia with aging, and cognitive decline in the elderly.\u0026nbsp; \u003Cbr\u003EConversely, treatment and consequent improvement of insulin resistance have been shown to result in better outcomes in virtually all of these conditions.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E *Criteria of Metabolic Syndrome:* \u003Cbr\u003ENCEP The US National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III (2001) requires at least three of the following:\u003Cbr\u003E• Central obesity: waist circumference ≥ 102 cm or 40 inches (male), ≥ 88 cm or 36 inches(female) \u003Cbr\u003E• Dyslipidemia: TG ≥ 1.7 mmol\/L (150 mg\/dl) \u003Cbr\u003E• Dyslipidemia: HDL-C \u0026lt; 40 mg\/dL (male), \u0026lt; 50 mg\/dL (female) \u003Cbr\u003E• Blood pressure ≥ 130\/85 mmHg \u003Cbr\u003E• Fasting plasma glucose ≥ 6.1 mmol\/L (110 mg\/dl) \u003Cbr\u003EIf BMI is \u0026gt;30kg\/m², central obesity can be assumed and waist circumference does not need to be measured.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EObesity is considered to be a disease of epidemic proportion. Metabolic syndrome is increasing in prevalence with obesity and sedentary lifestyles. Patients with metabolic syndrome frequently progress to type 2 DM and have increased risk for mortality and morbidity from cardiovascular diseases.\u003Cdiv\u003EHence there is a vital need for early\u0026nbsp; identification of patients with this syndrome and modification of risk factors to prevent further progression.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EAIM\u003C\/b\u003E:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETo assess the clinical spectrum,co morbidities and outcomes with obesity\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOBJECTIVES:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• To identify patients of obesity with and without comorbidities.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• To document associated comorbidities in patients with obesity in different age groups.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• To document outcomes in patients with patients.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESTUDY\u003C\/b\u003E \u003Cb\u003EDESIGN:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA Prospective Observational Study\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESTUDY PERIOD: \u003C\/b\u003E2 YEARS\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPLACE OF STUDY: \u003C\/b\u003EDepartment of General Medicine, Kamineni Institute of medical sciences Narketpalli.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESAMPLE SIZE: \u003C\/b\u003E5O PATIENTS\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMETHODOLOGY:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis is an observational study done in the department of general medicine where patients were screened for obesity with BMI, and those who satisfy the inclusion criteria were enrolled in the study after informing the nature of the study to the patients. Written informed consent was obtained from patients or guardian. Complete physical examination along with anthropometric measurements was done.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EFamily history of obesity, DM, hypertension (HT), cerebrovascular events, coronary artery disease, dyslipidemia (DL).\u0026nbsp; \u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EAnthropometry: Body weight was measured to the nearest 0.1 kg with a balance scale , and height was measured to the nearest 0.1 cm with stadiometer\u0026nbsp; with subjects lightly dressed and without shoes. Body mass index (BMI) was calculated as weight (kg) divided by height square (m2). \u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003ELaboratory investigations: Blood glucose, serum insulin and lipid levels were determined from blood samples taken after an overnight fast. \u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cbr\u003EBiochemical analysis and definition: Hyperinsulinemia is defined if fasting insulin \u0026gt;15mu\/L, HOMA IR \u0026gt; 3.5 HOMA IR is calculated as product of fasting plasma insulin in mu\/L and the fasting glucose in mg\/dl, divided by 405.Score of \u0026gt;3.5 is taken as insulin resistance and score \u0026lt; 3.5 as insulin sensitive. Fasting glucose \u0026gt;110mg\/dl is considered abnormal and \u0026gt;140mg\/dl is taken as having Diabetes mellitus Triglycerides \u0026gt;100mg\/dl, HDL \u0026lt; 40 mg\/dl is considered cut off. Metabolic syndrome was considered if three or more of the following criteria were present: BMI \u0026gt; 95th percentile, triglyceride \u0026gt;40mg\/dl, HDL \u0026lt;40mg\/dl, fasting glucose \u0026gt;110mg\/dl, systolic or diastolic BP \u0026gt;90th percentile.\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EINCLUSION CRITERIA:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Patients above 18 YEARS\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Patients presenting to our hospital\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;with waist circumference \u0026gt;102cm in\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;men and \u0026gt;88cm in women.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Patients with BMI greater than or\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;equal to 25.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EEXCLUSION CRITERIA:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E• \u003C\/b\u003EPatients less than 18 yrs\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Patients with waist circumference \u0026lt;102cms in men and \u0026lt;88cms in women\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Patients who doesnt want to be a part of study.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E• Mentally not competent to give consent.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOUTCOMES:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMorbidity\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EMortality\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ci\u003ECase
